text:
jamie: Quick PRD intake — customer asks for per-route latency/quality profiles. Problem: enterprise customers want to tune latency vs. output quality per API route (eg: search vs. completion) and have predictable cost. They need a knob that maps to routing + model variant selection and a rollout path with safety gates.

Key ask in one line: allow product teams to declare a small set of named profiles (e.g., fast, balanced, high_quality) that enforce target latency SLOs, minimum quality thresholds, and cost caps; system should route or pick model variants + batching config to satisfy the profile.

sanjay: couple clarifying q's: 1) Are profiles per-customer or global per-route with overrides? 2) Do we need soft targets (best-effort) vs hard-enforced guarantees? 3) What happens when profile can't be met (no capacity/model)?

jamie: answers: 1) primary req is per-route with per-tenant override (tenant can pin to profile or custom values). 2) start with soft targets + safety gates; GA may include stronger SLAs for Dedicated customers. 3) fallback behavior = prefer lower-cost compatible variant that meets minimum quality; if none, follow configured fallback (reject, queue, notify).

lia: Goals: 
- Enable product teams to pick/define profiles that map to measurable routing configs (latency p95, model variant, quantization level, batching window).
- Surface cost impact estimate in console and API before apply.
- Provide rollout strategy: canary by % or by tenant list + automatic rollback on quality regressions.
Non-goals: 
- Not building new model training or RL tuning. 
- Not guaranteeing hard latency SLAs for hosted free tier.
Success metrics (proposal): 
- 90% of customers using profiles can hit declared p95 within 2 weeks of apply (for Dedicated customers + supported regions).
- No more than 0.5% increase in customer-perceived quality regressions (eval-defined) after profile flips.
- Console adoption: X teams create a profile in first month (baseline TBD).

alex: Acceptance criteria / engineering checks: 
- API: create/update/get/delete profiles + assign per-route or per-tenant.  
- Runtime: routing policy yields deterministic choice given profile inputs, returns meta explaining decision. Example response header: `X-Profile-Decision: model=redwood-3b-q4_local,batching=20ms,expected_p95=120ms`
- Observability: per-profile telemetry (p95, p50, tokens/call, cost units) + alert on quality delta vs baseline.
- Rollout: must support staged rollout (weights) and automatic rollback rule: if eval-set quality drops > threshold for N windows, revert.

Edge cases alex calls out: 
- Mixed-route requests (batching across profiles) -> need deterministic arbitration (higher-latency profile wins or split requests). 
- Model variant incompatibility (function calling, tooling) — must advertise capability matrix and disallow selection. 
- Cold-start spikes for Dedicated scaling — need burst buffer or short-term fallback model.

marco: UX notes: console should show profile preview with cost delta and example latency curve. Quick path: create from template (fast/balanced/quality) or advanced editor with sliders. Also need explicit warning when rollback will impact customers. 

pm-bot: PRD checklist: [ ] problem statement, [ ] goals + non-goals, [ ] acceptance criteria, [ ] telemetry plan, [ ] rollout strategy, [ ] ownership + timeline. Tagging @lia as owner for next PRD draft. :robot_face:

sanjay: telemetry specifics: we need a per-profile synthetic / eval harness run during canary that checks sample prompts for regressions. Also require token-level cost estimate per profile and histogram of sequence lengths to pick batching windows.

lia: next steps: I'll draft a short PRD with the pieces above, include a sample API schema and console mockups. Owner: lia; Eng lead: sanjay; ML/quality: alex; Design: marco. Target: internal review in 5 business days, scope for alpha (Dedicated + Hosted beta) in 6 sprints. Anyone opposed or missing anything?

jamie: none from me. +1 to the timeline.

alex: will sketch the decision header + capability matrix this week.

sanjay: will prototype routing TTL and a fallback policy for cold starts.

lia: great — I'll create a PRD doc and link here when ready. :white_check_mark:
